# Generative and Style-based Models

Also called: 3D-aware NeRF, NeRF-GAN, Latent-NeRF

## Overview
Generative and Style-based Models extend NeRF from deterministic scene reconstruction to probabilistic 3D-aware image generation. They solve the problem of synthesizing novel views from a noise distribution or sparse inputs without requiring explicit camera poses or dense multi-view supervision, which is common in medical imaging or single-view datasets [S1, HyperNeRFGAN]. Unlike standard NeRF, which optimizes a single static field, these methods use GAN or diffusion objectives to enforce photorealistic priors and 3D consistency [S1, HyperNeRFGAN; S1, Latent-NeRF].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family compute a radiance field function $f_\theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ that outputs volume density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ (or latent features) for a query point $\mathbf{x}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}$. The final pixel color $\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{r})$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ is computed via the standard volume rendering integral:
$$
\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i
$$
where $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ and $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$. The architectural variations lie in how $\sigma_i$ and $\mathbf{c}_i$ are generated from the input coordinates, how the network is structured (depth, width, connectivity), and what auxiliary inputs (embeddings, priors, features) are fused into the computation.

## Subtopics

### HyperNeRFGAN
HyperNeRFGAN is a generative model that uses a hypernetwork to produce the weights of a simplified NeRF target network, trained using the StyleGAN2 objective to generate 3D representations from a Gaussian noise distribution [S1, HyperNeRFGAN]. It solves the problem of 3D-aware image generation when camera positions are unavailable or difficult to estimate, which is common in medical imaging and single-view datasets [S1, HyperNeRFGAN]. Unlike standard NeRF or conditioning-based GANs (e.g., GRAF, $\pi$-GAN) that require viewing directions or complex conditioning mechanisms, HyperNeRFGAN omits viewing direction inputs and uses Factorized Multiplicative Modulation (FMM) layers to inject noise-derived weights, enabling 3D consistency without explicit pose supervision [S1, HyperNeRFGAN].

### [Latent-NeRF](9110-latent-nerf.md)
Latent-NeRF is a method for optimizing Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) by integrating pre-trained latent diffusion models to improve novel view synthesis quality, particularly in scenarios with limited input data or for text-guided generation. It distinguishes itself from standard NeRF training by operating in a compact latent space rather than RGB space, using score distillation from a pre-trained autoencoder and diffusion model to guide the optimization. Unlike HyperNeRFGAN, which uses a GAN framework, Latent-NeRF leverages the denoising capabilities of diffusion models to enforce photorealistic priors.

### StyleNeRF
#### definition
StyleNeRF is a 3D-aware generative model that merges 3D scene representation with style-based generative models [S1, StyleNeRF].
#### step
StyleNeRF uses NeRF to generate low-resolution feature maps and samples them to high resolution to avoid super-computation volume rendering [S1, StyleNeRF]. It applies regularization terms to improve 3D consistency [S1, StyleNeRF].

## Background
Generative NeRF models emerged from the convergence of GANs and NeRF. Schwarz et al. [91] proposed GRAF in 2020, laying the foundation for conditional radiance fields. Niemeyer et al. [92] introduced GIRAFFE in 2021 for compositional scene generation. Chan et al. [93] proposed $\pi$-GAN in 2021 for high-quality 3D-aware synthesis. Gu et al. [96] proposed StyleNeRF in 2022, integrating style-based generation with 3D fields [S1]. These methods address the lack of high-quality image synthesis in earlier NeRF-GAN hybrids, which were limited to simple geometric objects like faces and cars [S1].
